{{Navbar-Global Gas Infrastructure Tracker}}
'''Texas Eastern Transmission (TETCO) Gas Pipeline''' is an operating natural gas pipeline with additional expansions that are proposed and operating.<ref name=source1>[http://bit.ly/2rDChwc Texas Eastern Transmission (TETCO) Gas Pipeline,] Enbridge website, accessed January 2018</ref>

==Location==
The pipeline runs from the Gulf of Mexico in Texas and Louisiana up through Mississippi, Arkansas, Tennessee, Missouri, Kentucky, Illinois, Indiana, Ohio, and Pennsylvania to deliver gas in the New York City area.

==Background==
Texas Eastern Transmission (TETCO) is operated by Texas Eastern Transmission, LP, which is owned by Enbridge.<ref>[https://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/private/snapshot.asp?privcapId=3033869 Company Overview of Texas Eastern Transmission, LP], Bloomberg, accessed January 2018</ref>

Spectra Energy and Conocophillips have proposed a joint expansion project called the TEMAX Project that would add 33 miles of pipeline to the system, stretching from Clarington, Ohio to Delta, Pennsylvania. It would add 395 million cubic feet per day of capacity and cost $500 million. The project includes construction of pipeline, looping and replacement of compressor stations and is is preparing to pre-file with FERC.<ref>[https://s3.amazonaws.com/pgj-wp-media/wp-content/uploads/2018/10/PN1018-Planned-Projects.pdf Planned Projects], Pipeline News, accessed October 2018</ref>

In January of 2019 an explosion in the pipeline injured two people and destroyed two homes in Noble County, Ohio.<ref>[https://globalnews.ca/news/4872878/enbridge-pipeline-explosion-ohio/ Enbridge pipeline explosion in Ohio damages homes, sends flames shooting into sky], Global News, accessed January 2019</ref>
===TEMAX Pipeline Expansion===
In 2008, Spectra and ConocoPhillips announced a proposed pipeline called the TEMAX Pipeline. Gas would run through the TETCO Pipeline system, forming an agreement to deliver up to 395 million cubic feet per day of Rocky Mountain natural gas to the U.S. Northeast through the planned pipeline expansion. The expansion will start in Clarington, Ohio, running through Spectra’s Texas Eastern Transmission pipeline system to Delta, Pennsylvania.<ref>[https://www.reuters.com/article/spectra-conoco-idUSWNAS487720080521 Spectra, Conoco in Rockies gas shipment pact], Reuters, May 21, 2008</ref><ref>[https://s3.amazonaws.com/pgj-wp-media/wp-content/uploads/2018/10/PN1018-Planned-Projects.pdf Planned Pipelines], Pipeline News, accessed October 2018</ref>

There have been no development updates since 2008 and the project is presumed to be cancelled. 
===Texas Eastern Appalachia to Market (TEAM) 2012 Expansion===
In October 2008, TETCO held an open season for the TEAM expansion project.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://waytogoto.com/wiki/index.php/Texas_Eastern_Appalachia_to_Market|title=Texas Eastern Appalachia to Market - Wikimarcellus|website=waytogoto.com|language=en|access-date=2023-08-30}}</ref> In September 2011, FERC published the environmental assessment of Texas Eastern Appalachia to Market 2012 Expansion Project. The project involved installation of 17.3 miles of 36-inch-diameter natural gas transmission pipeline in Greene, Fayette, Franklin, Adams and Fulton Counties, Pennsylvania. TETCO also proposed to abandon approximately 11.3 miles of 24-inch-diameter  pipeline in Franklin and Adams Counties, Pennsylvania.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2011/09/02/2011-22517/texas-eastern-transmission-lp-notice-of-availability-of-the-environmental-assessment-for-the|title=Federal Register :: Request Access|website=www.federalregister.gov|language=en|access-date=2023-08-30}}</ref> In October 2012, TETCO completed the expansion.

=== Texas Eastern Appalachia to Market (TEAM) 2014 Expansion ===
In November 2014, TETCO completed TETCO TEAM 2014 expansion. TEAM 2014 involved construction of approximately 33.4 miles of 36-inch-diameter natural gas transmission pipeline comprised of seven separate pipeline loops in Pennsylvania, and modification of existing pipeline facilities in Pennsylvania, West Virginia, Ohio, Kentucky, Tennessee, Alabama, and Mississippi.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2012/10/15/2012-25206/texas-eastern-transmission-lp-notice-of-intent-to-prepare-an-environmental-assessment-for-the-texas|title=Federal Register :: Request Access|website=www.federalregister.gov|language=en|access-date=2023-08-30}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hartenergy.com/news/spectra-energy-names-team-2014-expansion-anchor-shippers-54422|title=Spectra Energy Names TEAM 2014 Expansion Anchor Shippers|last=|first=|date=13 April, 2012|website=Hart Energy|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=30 August, 2023}}</ref>

=== Texas Eastern Appalachia to Market (TEAM) 2021 Expansion ===
In November 2021, TETCO completed the installation of additional looping on the segment in Westmoreland, Berks, Fayette counties, Pennsylvania.
===Ohio Pipeline Energy Network (OPEN) Gas Pipeline===
The pipeline runs from Columbiana County, Ohio, to Monroe County, Ohio.

In December 2011, Chesapeake Energy, American Electric Power and Spectra Energy Corp announced a pipeline expansion of the Texas Eastern system, connecting Utica and Marcellus shale in Ohio to markets in East and South.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.dispatch.com/story/business/2011/12/23/new-pipeline-to-carry-ohio/23620894007/|title=New pipeline to carry Ohio gas|work=The Columbus Dispatch|access-date=2023-08-28|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pgjonline.com/magazine/2012/january-2012-vol-239-no-1/projects/texas-eastern-to-develop-ohio-pipeline-energy-network-project|title=Texas Eastern To Develop Ohio Pipeline Energy Network Project|website=pgjonline.com|access-date=2023-08-28}}</ref> U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission approved the project on 02 December, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.psgincs.com/ohio-gulf-coast-pipeline-approval/|title=Ohio Gulf Coast Pipeline Project Approved|last=|first=|date=03 December, 2021|website=www.psgincs.com|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2023-08-28}}</ref>  Ohio Pipeline Energy Network project was originally scheduled to become operational in November 2015, but the mainline portion of the project, which is the reverse flow along part of the existing TETCO mainline began service in mid-September.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.spglobal.com/commodityinsights/en/ci/research-analysis/pipelines-pace-north-american-natural-gas-production-growth.html|title=Sharing insights elevates their impact|date=2015-09-22|work=S&P Global|access-date=2023-08-28}}</ref>

===Texas Eastern Appalachian Lease (TEAL) Gas Pipeline===

The extension would begin near the village of Bern, Ohio and turn north at Clarington, Ohio.

The Texas Eastern Appalachian Lease (TEAL) pipeline would be operated by Texas Eastern Transmission, LP, which is owned by Enbridge.<ref>[https://www.enbridge.com/projects-and-infrastructure/projects/texas-eastern-appalachian-lease-project Texas Eastern Appalachian Lease Project], Enbridge, accessed January 2018.</ref> The TEAL project would include installation of a 4.4-mile pipeline loop in Ohio,  a 1,790 feet of pipeline to connect with the Nexus Gas Transmission pipeline in Ohio, and additional natural gas compressor facilities in Ohio.<ref>[https://www.permits.performance.gov/projects/nexus-gas-transmission-teal-dte-lease-and-vector-lease-n Nexus Gas Transmission, TEAL, DTE Lease, and Vector Lease], Permitting Dashboard, accessed January 2018</ref>

The Phase 1 and Phase 2 of the expansion project was completed in November 2018 and April 2019, respectively, beginning service in 2018 and 2019.<ref name="eg">[https://www.energyglobal.com/pipelines/project-news/25102018/plans-to-put-into-service-remainder-of-teal-gas-pipeline/ Plans to put into service remainder of TEAL gas pipeline], World Pipelines, Oct. 25, 2018</ref><ref name=":2" />
===Cameron Expansion Project===
In 2019, Texas Eastern Transmission applied for an expansion project in Louisiana called the Cameron Expansion Project.<ref name=":2" /> According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, as of April 2021 the project had been approved but had not yet entered construction.<ref name=":2" /> In September 2021 it was reported that the project was under construction and would be commissioned within two months.<ref>[https://pgjonline.com/news/2021/september/enbridge-s-cameron-extension-pipeline-project-nearing-completion Enbridge’s Cameron Extension Pipeline Project Nearing Completion], Pipeline & Gas Journal, Sep. 14, 2021</ref> The project was completed in December 2021.<ref name=":2" />
===Middlesex Expansion Project===
The expansion project interconnects with the [[Transcontinental Gas Pipeline|Transco Gas Pipeline]] and the Transco Gas Pipeline's Woodbridge Lateral, ultimately delivering natural gas to 725 MW Woodbridge Energy Center combined cycle power plant. The expanded capacity is in New Jersey, USA. Developers have applied with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.<ref name=eia/>

According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, as of April 2021 the project was under construction.<ref name="eia" /> It was completed in September 2021.<ref name="eia" />

=== Venice Extension Project ===

The extension project is intended to expand TETCO's infrastructure to connect to facilitate delivery to [[Plaquemines LNG Terminal]] and better connect to Gulf Coast LNG export markets.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.enbridge.com/projects-and-infrastructure/projects/venice-extension-project|title=https://www.enbridge.com/projects-and-infrastructure/projects/venice-extension-project|last=|first=|date=|website=|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>

=== Appalachia to Market III Project ===
The proposed Appalachia to Market III Project is designed to provide additional natural gas supply in Pennsylvania and the broader region to meet growing demand from utilities and industrial users for affordable, reliable, domestic energy. The Project proposes an expansion of the existing Texas Eastern Transmission (Texas Eastern) system by replacing approximately 2 miles of 24-inch diameter pipeline with 36-inch diameter pipeline, retire and remove an existing receiver site, construct a new receiver site, and make modifications at the Bedford Compressor Station.<ref name="eia" />
